adventure.title: The Siege of the Stone Lung
adventure.synopsis: On the nineteenth day of the siege, Kest Mourne's right gate tower splits from parapet to foundation and the civic lantern above the Pale Gardens burns blue. The Host of the Lower Road has closed every caravan route and driven sappers beneath the walls. First Warden Ilyra Dain answers with a temporary six-lantern commission: cross the city's defensive sectors, spend its last reserves where they can still matter, and carry field truth back into command before the Stone Lung reaches its next crisis.
adventure.premise: An Underdark city is failing by sectors while an enemy host times its assaults to the strokes of the ancient engine that gives the city air. A local, foreign, or mixed company receives bounded authority across six fronts. It must buy military time, distinguish sabotage from structural failure, uncover the old theft beneath the siege, and decide what survival obliges Kest Mourne to restore.
adventure.explanation: The Host came for the Stone Lung, not Kest Mourne's streets. Eighteen years ago, a lethal mold blight forced Kest Mourne to seal the engine's southern branch, cutting the settlement of Lorn away from most of its fresh-air exchange. The quarantine was justified; what followed was not. The blight died, the promised purge and filter works were abandoned, and the council made the closure permanent while falsifying the conduit maps. Lorn survived on auxiliary chimneys until its last reliable shaft collapsed six weeks ago. Marshal Sera Venn sent the original Lorn conduit plate and demanded a joint inspection. Kest Mourne called it a forgery and sealed it beside the old minutes. Venn now intends to seize the Lung and compel a controlled reopening. Her chief engineer, Korr Bas, holds wartime technical command over the Host's resonance corps once its crews reach their work. Certain that delay is another death sentence for Lorn, he has hidden a larger yield and issued Heartstrike orders beyond Venn's limits. Methane-rich black breath has gathered behind the southern masonry; the charge will ignite it and drive flame through the deep galleries of both cities. The commission must keep Kest Mourne alive long enough to expose the old decision, separate Venn's enforceable claim from Bas's catastrophe, and settle whether the Lung will be closed, sacrificed, or made to breathe for both settlements again.

references.title: First Warden Ilyra Dain
references.summary: Kest Mourne's First Warden, a siege commander who lets verified facts reverse orders and whose six-lantern commission crosses sectors without replacing civil or technical authority.
references.content:
## Six flames, one bounded writ

First Warden Ilyra Dain commands Kest Mourne's defense from the Lantern Court. Her six-lantern commission exists because ordinary command stops at sector boundaries while bombardment, air, food, water, and evacuation do not. The writ permits cross-sector movement, bounded requisitions, emergency reallocations, prisoner exchanges, evacuations, and temporary parleys. It does not permit surrender, punishment of civilians, permanent transfer of the Stone Lung, or a technical order that competent crews judge impossible.

## A fact must become an order

Ilyra inherited false infrastructure records rather than the decision that made them. She will spend lives to hold defensible ground, but she distrusts gestures that only look resolute. A report matters to her when its source can be tested, its cost can be named, and its conclusion can alter work already under way. She can reverse an order without pretending the first order was wise.

## Emergency command is not ownership

Siege law lets Ilyra direct available reserves, order evacuation and exchange, and bind a temporary operational compact. Permanent joint control of the Lung requires civil process, public records, and recognized Lorn witnesses. Her current orders, allocations, disclosure decision, reserve movement, compact, and willingness to parley remain live adventure state.

references.title: Speaker Edda Marr
references.summary: The civil-council speaker who guards Kest Mourne's sealed blight minutes and embodies the difference between a private admission and a correction the whole city must obey.
references.content:
## Minutes beneath the council seal

Speaker Edda Marr leads Kest Mourne's civil council. She is the granddaughter of a magistrate who ordered the southern seal during the mold blight and knows that a secret public work was performed. She has protected the sealed minutes because she believes disclosure during a siege would fracture the city and vindicate the Host. Her fear about timing is serious; her defense of concealment is still wrong.

## Six copies or rumor

Kest Mourne does not admit a civic fact through one officer's remorse. A correction becomes operative when it enters all six sector ledgers, travels down the command tubes, changes the wall map, and is allowed to alter an order already killing people. Edda's office can release council records and make that civil acknowledgment possible. It cannot make an unexecuted confession binding by itself.

## Civil authority under bombardment

Edda can speak for council procedure, custody of its records, and the public acts by which the city corrects its own account. She does not command the Host, the Gate line, or the Stone Lung's technical crews, and she cannot settle permanent joint control alone. Her current custody, release, reading, copying, publication, and use of the sealed minutes remain live adventure state.

references.title: Ventwright Tamar Ohn
references.summary: Kest Mourne's senior ventwright, responsible for technically executable work on the Stone Lung and entitled to refuse commands that surviving crews and machinery cannot safely perform.
references.content:
## An engine known by repairs

Ventwright Tamar Ohn maintains the accessible parts of the Stone Lung and the civic systems coupled to its strokes. She knows the machine through replaced bearings, improvised braces, seasonal draft, crew habits, and failures absent from formal diagrams. Her authority comes from reproducible work rather than reverence for inherited plans.

## Name the sequence and the crew

Tamar treats every remedy as an ordered operation: measure, isolate, brace, vent, move people, turn a control, and verify the next stroke. A military or civil command cannot make missing tools, labor, breathing protection, or pressure limits appear. The six-lantern writ expressly preserves a competent crew's right to reject a technically impossible order.

## Competence is not sovereignty

Tamar can judge whether machinery can survive an intervention, organize qualified operators, and state the material conditions a plan requires. She does not own the Lung, decide Lorn's political claim, or command soldiers merely because engineers need a road held. Her current diagnosis, recommendation, measurements, keys, available crew, and chosen remedy remain live adventure state.

references.title: Gate Captain Brann Sile
references.summary: The captain responsible for the Shattered Gate, whose practical military authority is measured in defensible ground, named reserves, and minutes bought for the rest of Kest Mourne.
references.content:
## Minutes held in stone and bodies

Gate Captain Brann Sile commands the defenders assigned to Kest Mourne's outer gate. He reads the siege in frontage, trapped crews, usable stairs, reserve movement, and how long a shortened line can still protect the inner roads. He has little patience for a claim that removes people from the wall without naming what their absence buys.

## Proof that changes the line

Brann will cooperate with investigation when it solves an immediate military problem: predicts an assault, rescues a crew, identifies a false withdrawal, or gives him defensible room to abandon stone before people. Clear orders and verified battlefield intelligence matter more to him than rank performed at a distance.

## A gate command, not a city command

Brann can command his assigned soldiers, receive and guard battlefield prisoners, report the condition of the outer line, and execute lawful reserve or withdrawal orders. He cannot allocate every city resource, overrule competent technical refusal, or decide the Lung's permanent control. His current line, withdrawal, prisoners, reserve, report, casualties, and gate condition remain live adventure state.

references.title: Marshal Sera Venn
references.summary: Commander of the Host of the Lower Road, pursuing enforceable access to the Stone Lung while retaining strategic authority distinct from Korr Bas's narrower technical command.
references.content:
## The claim behind the siege

Marshal Sera Venn commands the Host of the Lower Road. Lorn's last reliable auxiliary chimney failed after years of decline under a supposedly temporary southern seal. Venn sent Kest Mourne an original conduit plate and demanded joint inspection; the city rejected it under the authority of its own false map. She chose siege and controlled seizure rather than accept another refusal.

## Access that cannot be withdrawn

Venn's objective is enforceable access to the Stone Lung, not friendship with Kest Mourne and not indiscriminate extermination. She recognizes prisoner exchange and bounded local truces, but a promise made while one city retains every control does not answer Lorn's claim. Public records, divided custody, mixed crews, and physical access can create leverage that survives the emergency.

## Strategic command and its limit

Venn may direct Host units, negotiate ceasefire corridors, exchange prisoners, and authenticate strategic orders or revocations. The Host's wartime articles nevertheless give qualified engineers technical authority once their crews reach assigned work, creating a boundary Korr Bas can exploit. Her current assault, truce, revocation, negotiation, access demand, unit position, and operational cooperation remain live adventure state.

references.title: Engineer Korr Bas
references.summary: The Host's chief resonance engineer, who converted bounded technical command into the valid-looking Heartstrike overreach he considers preferable to Lorn's continued suffocation.
references.content:
## Lorn measured in failed breaths

Engineer Korr Bas designed the Host's resonance weapons and survived Lorn's worst air failures. He believes Kest Mourne will preserve its monopoly whenever uncertainty makes delay defensible. He is lucid about the danger behind the southern seal and still judges catastrophic force preferable to watching Lorn disappear by degrees.

## A countermand shaped like necessity

Under the Host's wartime articles, Bas controls calibration and firing procedure after a qualified resonance crew reaches its assigned work. He has stretched that narrow authority into a valid-looking countermand, concealed a larger yield from strategic command, and named the resulting Heartstrike plan a technical necessity. His leverage depends on isolated communications and crews who can plausibly mistake overreach for lawful duty.

## Technical command is not the war aim

Bas can direct assigned resonance crews and determine the calibration and firing sequence of their weapons. He cannot define Venn's strategic objective, bind a truce, settle control of the Lung, or make mutual destruction lawful by calling it engineering. His current location, command reach, firing authority, charge state, countermand, signal, and fate remain live adventure state.

references.title: The Six-Lantern Commission
references.summary: Kest Mourne's bounded emergency writ, allowing one company to carry verified facts and finite resources across sector boundaries without inheriting surrender, punishment, permanent-control, or impossible technical powers.
references.content:
## Six flames on one copied writ

Ordinary authority in Kest Mourne stops at sector boundaries. The six-lantern commission lets one proven company cross those boundaries while the city is under siege. Copies go to all six principal sectors so a field decision can be recognized without pretending the company has replaced the officers, crews, and civil bodies already there.

## What crosses a sector line

The writ permits cross-sector movement, bounded requisitions, emergency reallocations, prisoner exchanges, evacuations, and temporary parleys. Sector leaders may demand reasons and remain answerable for execution. A verified fact can therefore release a reserve, redirect material, protect a witness, or make a local truce executable before ordinary council procedure catches up.

## What ink cannot create

The commission does not permit surrender, punishment of civilians, permanent transfer of the Stone Lung, or technical work that competent crews judge impossible. Ink cannot summon soldiers, tools, breathing hoods, witnesses, roads, or cooperation. Who carries a copy, what it has already moved, which officer accepts it, and whether a compact survives are decided in play.

references.title: The Lantern Court
references.summary: Kest Mourne's public command floor, where six sector lanterns, casualty boards, wall maps, runners, ledgers, and command tubes turn verified field facts into witnessed citywide orders.
references.content:
## A command floor that breathes

The Lantern Court stands beneath six iron lanterns, one for each principal defensive sector. Their flames narrow and brighten with the Stone Lung's cycle. Casualty boards, sector tokens, the wall map, material tallies, and arriving runners make the city's competing needs visible in one public room.

## A fact becomes work

The Court is where evidence enters command. A damaged object needs judgment; a report contradicts the map under the officers' feet; a messenger spends a final sentence on one usable fact. Kest Mourne recognizes a civic correction when it reaches the sector ledgers, travels down the command tubes, alters the wall map, and changes an order already costing lives.

## Six lanterns cannot summon hands

The Court can compare claims and send recognized orders through the city. It cannot make one crew serve two sectors, turn rumor into proof, or restore authority by holding another briefing. The boards, tokens, runners, ledgers, orders, and even the Court's remaining coherence change with the siege.

references.title: The Shattered Gate
references.summary: Kest Mourne's principal outer defense, joining towers, galleries, inner turns, signal positions, and the upper-city road through which military time and a movable reserve reach the rest of the siege.
references.content:
## The city measured in minutes

The Shattered Gate is Kest Mourne's principal outer approach. Its doors, paired towers, northern gallery, inner turns, stairs, signal positions, and upper-city road make one defensive system. Holding or yielding any part changes how long soldiers, engineers, wounded, and orders can still move through the city.

## A wall that protects other work

The Gate matters beyond the stone it occupies. Braces and iron come from the Foundry. Assault timings can arrive from captured lower-road records. A reserve held here may instead escort a technical crew or contest the Stone Lung. The Gate's military value is therefore time, controlled withdrawal, and a road kept usable for another obligation.

## The map cannot hold the breach

The record fixes doors, towers, galleries, turns, stairs, signals, and the upper road. It does not say which tower stands, where defenders have withdrawn, whether prisoners were taken, or how much reserve remains. Damage, crews, casualties, enemy access, signals, and the defensive outcome belong to the current siege.

references.title: The Cinder Foundry
references.summary: Kest Mourne's three-hall forge and repair works, coupling gate braces, pumps, filters, counterweights, tuned tools, skilled labor, and the Foundry gantry into one finite production system.
references.content:
## Three halls around a red chimney

The Cinder Foundry descends through three working halls around a chimney of red stone. It casts gate braces, repairs pumps, shapes filter housings, maintains the Stone Lung's counterweights, and keeps the tuning benches used for precise resonance work. The east furnace and upper gantry connect production directly to the city's defense and breathing engine.

## One shift cannot become four

Foundry work is an allocation of skilled hands, heat, iron, benches, and safe cadence. Straight beams can reinforce the Gate, tuned wedges can reach Heartstrike, counterweights can support retuning, and frames can carry living filters. Each program has different tools and tolerances; dividing one shift produces diminished packages rather than additional labor.

## Nothing leaves the floor by description

The Foundry's durable capacity is heat, iron, benches, skilled cadence, and its roads to other sectors. A sheet cannot say whether the furnace is safe, a shell remains buried, benches survived, iron is available, or a crew accepted an order. What is completed, diminished, abandoned, or actually delivered to the Stone Lung is settled in play.

references.title: The Pale Gardens
references.summary: Kest Mourne's food and living-filter terraces, where rootstock, spores, insects, service vents, and ward connections preserve a biological record of airflow that mechanical plans can miss.
references.content:
## Food that reads the air

The Pale Gardens descend beneath curtains of white fungus. Their terraces feed Kest Mourne and clean air returning from crowded wards. Rootstock, spore color, moisture, cave insects, and the timing of growth against the Stone Lung's stroke make the Gardens a living instrument as well as a food source.

## Two failures can share one bed

Sabotage follows hands, carts, tools, and sheds. Structural airflow failure forms gradients across beds and vents. The Gardens' stable value lies in preserving enough living material to separate those causes, map ward-by-ward flow, and produce filters for other sectors. Their old southern stock also preserves relationships erased from later civic plans.

## Biology does not choose the remedy

The Gardens can expose patterns and provide living material. They cannot name every saboteur, order a burn, allocate workers, authenticate a witness, or prove which vent is safe now. Contamination, harvest, surviving filters, readings, crews, quarantine, and loss must be discovered in the beds.

references.title: The Refuge Galleries
references.summary: Processional galleries converted to civic refuge, joining relief records, the memorial wall, family tablets, an old service door, and the memorial stair to the Stone Lung's southern controls.
references.content:
## Processional stone under ordinary need

The Refuge Galleries were built for civic processions. Their reliefs, broad stairs, lower halls, service doors, and water connections make them a natural shelter when the upper city fails. Relief stewards keep air, water, ration, illness, and movement records close to the people those numbers describe.

## The memorial preserves a road

The public wall names citizens killed during the mold blight. Family tablets around an older service door preserve additional workers and arrange the first signs as a ventwright mark. Behind the memorial crypt, a narrow stair descends toward the Stone Lung's southern controls. Grief retained geography that official maps removed.

## Shelter does not settle testimony

The Galleries can gather witnesses, records, evacuation labor, and a road below. They do not decide who has arrived, whose testimony holds, whether records are released, which families move, or whether the memorial stair remains usable. Crowd pressure, rations, air, custody, routes, and civic standing change with the emergency.

references.title: The Cisterns of Black Breath
references.summary: Kest Mourne's oldest water works, combining public pools, lower valves, an inspection arch, overflow routes, and a maintenance channel whose stonework reaches the hidden southern exchange system.
references.content:
## Water above, old works below

The Cisterns of Black Breath lie beneath Kest Mourne's oldest wards. Upper pools feed public pumps; lower pools, sluices, numbered valves, inspection arches, drains, and overflow galleries control what reaches the city below. The fourth pool meets deliberate southern masonry where later maps claim natural stone.

## One buried system carries air and water

A maintenance channel behind the lower works opens toward the old lower road. Air and water move through it in opposite phases. The cistern geometry therefore joins public supply, the southern seal, the Stone Lung, and a route toward the Countermine. Breathing protection, measured hammer signals, and valve order matter because haste can move poison or dead air into occupied wards.

## No plan shows today's water

The record preserves pools, sluices, valves, arches, drains, overflow, and the old southern masonry. It cannot certify today's water, gas pressure, trapped crew, breathing hoods, valve position, readings, overflow capacity, enemy access, or a safe vent. Those must be measured below the waterline.

references.title: The Countermine
references.summary: The defensive excavation where Kest Mourne's miners meet an older lower road, Host sapper works, signal routes, and the most direct military approach to Heartstrike and the Stone Lung.
references.content:
## A road found by digging toward hammers

The Countermine begins as Kest Mourne's answer to enemy sappers and reaches an older lower road omitted from current maps. Its galleries connect mine faces, collapse chambers, signal routes, prisoner exchange points, and the direct approach to the Stone Lung's charge gallery.

## Every command must cross the tunnel

The lower road carries more than troops. Assault schedules, firing instructions, revocations, relay pulses, wounded, prisoners, and technical crews all depend on a passage that can be blocked, deceived, collapsed, or held. The Countermine is where military, technical, and political command occupy the same narrow geometry.

## Orders narrow inside the gallery

The record fixes the lower-road connections and the command routes that depend on them. It cannot settle the current collapse, cable, signals, prisoners, truce, sapper allegiance, access to Venn, charge readiness, or control of the approach. Every one of those questions is live in the tunnel.

references.title: The Stone Lung
references.summary: The pre-imperial pressure engine beneath Kest Mourne, whose vanes, geothermal throat, counterweights, branches, southern controls, and three military approaches exchange air between Kest Mourne and Lorn.
references.content:
## Stone that takes a breath

The Stone Lung fills a pressure vault beneath Kest Mourne. Curved vanes of porous rock flex around a geothermal throat while counterweights climb and fall above them. Each stroke draws through one set of branches and releases through another, moving air, dust, flame, cloth, and pressure across both settlements.

## Three roads enter one machine

The Foundry gantry reaches the crown, counterweights, and charge harmonics. The memorial stair reaches the old civic platform and southern manual controls. The Countermine gallery reaches the lower-road assault and charge works. Each is a military road capable of carrying crews, witnesses, orders, tools, wounded, and armed bodies—not merely an entrance.

## Machinery is not sovereignty

The Lung was built to balance more than one branch, but its physical capacity does not determine who may command, inspect, repair, or control it. Current pressure, open branches, keys, approach control, crews, Heartstrike, damage, remedy, and the final transfer of the controls belong to the finale.

references.title: The Host of the Lower Road
references.summary: Lorn's siege army, combining shield companies, sappers, scouts, signal crews, and resonance engineers under strategic command whose wartime articles preserve a narrower technical chain.
references.content:
## An army raised for access

The Host of the Lower Road is Lorn's siege force. Shield companies fix defenders at the wall; sappers and scouts work the buried approaches; signal crews connect dispersed commands; resonance engineers make stone itself part of the assault. Its strategic objective is enforceable access to the Stone Lung rather than possession of every street in Kest Mourne.

## Two chains inside one command

Marshal authority sets the war aim, unit movement, exchanges, and strategic limits. The Host's wartime articles give qualified engineers bounded control over calibration and firing procedure after their crews reach assigned work. That separation protects technical competence and also creates room for a valid-looking overreach when communications fail or necessity is falsely claimed.

## Doctrine does not place a soldier

The record fixes the Host's formations and divided command, not the position of any company or the authority of any current message. Assaults, signals, prisoners, truces, revocations, crew loyalty, access, casualties, and Lorn's settlement posture change with play.

references.title: The Sealed Blight Minutes
references.summary: Kest Mourne's sealed council record of the mold emergency, temporary southern closure, expected harm to Lorn, planned purge and filter works, and later decision to preserve the closure after the blight ended.
references.content:
## A lawful emergency written down

The sealed minutes record a real lethal mold blight and the council's decision to close the Stone Lung's southern branch as quarantine. They also record that the closure would cut Lorn's air exchange and that purge beds, filters, and later reopening were part of the emergency plan.

## The later decision in the same hand

Subsequent entries preserve the choice that changed quarantine into policy: the contaminated strain died, promised works were abandoned, workers were reassigned, and the southern closure was kept while the public map and civic account ceased to show the branch. The minutes distinguish an initially justified act from the concealed permanence that followed.

## A record is not a public correction

The minutes preserve what a council wrote; they do not open their own seal. Who holds, reads, copies, publishes, believes, or acts on them is current state. Until witnesses and command procedure give the record effect, it remains evidence rather than correction.

references.title: The Original Lorn Conduit Plate
references.summary: An original technical plate from Lorn showing the shared southern exchange system and the old relationship among Lorn, Kest Mourne's lower works, and the Stone Lung.
references.content:
## Lines cut before the map was changed

The original Lorn conduit plate depicts a southern exchange joining Lorn, Kest Mourne's lower water and vent works, and the Stone Lung. Its measurements, maker's conventions, valve marks, and branch geometry predate the later civic map that shows natural stone where the southern works should be.

## A demand for inspection, not surrender

Lorn preserved the plate after its auxiliary chimneys began to fail. It supports a demand that both settlements inspect the old controls together and explains why a promise of future air is weaker than physical access, divided custody, and records neither city can quietly erase. The plate does not itself settle permanent control.

## Engraving must meet the stone

The plate can be tested against masonry, valve numbers, rootstock, pressure readings, and surviving score marks. It does not determine who possesses it, whether a copy is authentic, which audience accepts it, what inspection or publication follows, or what order and legal effect result. Its force comes from comparison and use in the current crisis.

references.title: Heartstrike
references.summary: The Host's resonance operation for fracturing the Stone Lung's southern seal during release, built from tuned shells, ceramic ribs, cables, relays, governors, and a manual firing path.
references.content:
## A siege weapon tuned to a breath

Heartstrike is a resonance operation rather than one loose explosive. Tuned shells and wedges establish the frequency; ceramic ribs store and return vibration; a braided cable and relay chain carry the firing pulse toward the southern seal; governors and a manual path control when the accumulated force is released.

## Fracture is not controlled reopening

The operation is designed to break the southern masonry during the Stone Lung's release. A bounded version might expose the branch for seizure. A larger yield can mix pressure, heat, and methane-rich black breath into an ignition that travels through both settlements. Strategic authorization, technical calibration, and the physical ability to fire are distinct forms of control.

## The weapon exists before the countdown

The record fixes Heartstrike's architecture and danger, not its readiness. Placement, charge, cable continuity, governor state, firing signal, manual access, crew obedience, Bas's location and command reach, Venn's knowledge, and whether the weapon survives belong to the current siege.

encounters.title: The Lantern Court
encounters.summary: Six civic lanterns breathe above a command floor where every allocation saves one sector by exposing another.
encounters.opening_view: Before Ilyra Dain finishes reading the six-lantern commission, a clerk scrapes three names from the Shattered Gate board and writes nine beneath them. The Gardens lantern gutters blue. A cistern runner sets an oily flask beside a ringing shell fragment and the city's last unassigned iron. Six officers reach for the same spears, beams, hoods, and demolition cart. Ilyra hands over the copied writ and turns every sector token to contested. The Stone Lung exhales; one token must turn toward help before the flames steady.
encounters.content:
## Arrival

On the nineteenth morning, the Pale Gardens lantern gutters blue just as a runner from the Shattered Gate asks for every uncommitted spear. Casualty clerks are still scraping yesterday's names from the boards. First Warden Ilyra Dain lays six copies of an emergency writ across the sector map and asks the company to carry decisions where ordinary command cannot.

## The six-lantern commission

Choose why this local, foreign, or mixed company can cross lines that stop ordinary officers: local defenders trusted in several wards, specialists trapped inside the encirclement, envoys whose road home has closed, mercenaries whose contract has become a civic obligation, or a mixed company already proven under pressure. The writ names no profession, company title, or prescribed route.

Its copies authorize cross-sector movement, bounded requisitions, emergency reallocations, prisoner exchanges, evacuations, and temporary parleys. They do not authorize surrender, punishment of civilians, permanent transfer of the Lung, or technical work a competent crew judges impossible. A sector leader may demand reasons and remains answerable for carrying the order out. The commission lets a verified fact cross the city, but it works only when the company brings a workable allocation with it; parchment cannot supply missing crews, roads, or hours.

## Command under pressure

Nothing here happens in private. Messengers shoulder past one another. Casualty boards are scraped and rewritten before the families of the dead. Every allocation has witnesses and losers. Speaker Edda Marr urges silence around the old wards. Gate officers demand reserves. Ventwright Tamar Ohn asks for machinery already promised to military repair. Refuge stewards ask how much air command can guarantee; no officer gives them a number.

On each return, bring two or three demands to the same table. A useful first collision is:

- Captain Brann Sile asks for the iron reserve before the Lung's next exhalation.
- The Cinder Foundry asks whether its last straight beams belong at the Gate or beneath a damaged ventilation frame.
- The Refuge Galleries report that a former vent mason is telling the crowd Kest Mourne stole another settlement's air.

An allocation changes conditions; it does not close a location. Soldiers sent to the Gate reduce casualties there and leave the cistern crews exposed. The demolition cart can open the Countermine or remove a live shell from the Foundry, not both. Name the people who receive the order and the people who lose it.

## The siege ledger

Mark each sector **contested**, **held**, or **breached**. A clean resolution holds the sector and preserves its full finale asset. A costly resolution holds it with a diminished asset. Abandonment or decisive failure breaches it and applies the encounter's **If neglected** result.

Whenever the commission returns to the Court—or after two field sectors without a return—report one benefit from a held sector and one worsening elsewhere. The Gate releases a reserve. The Foundry sends braces. Refuge stewards form an evacuation crew. Elsewhere, a shell buries the tuning benches, a ration cut starts a crush, or the lower sluice gives way. While the commission works one front, the others keep moving.

Early reconnaissance at the Stone Lung does not by itself begin Heartstrike. Start the three-stroke finale when Bas detects an attempt to seize the charge gallery, sever the main firing cable, or move the southern valves; when his plan has been exposed and another major opportunity lets him act; or when three breached sectors complete his assault route. A peripheral relay cut, hidden watch, or study of the crown may delay or mislead him instead. Give a full-cycle warning. Do not begin before an approach to the Lung has been established, and never resolve Heartstrike offscreen. Table time spent on careful work is not siege time unless the fiction changes.

## Ilyra at the table

Ilyra will reverse a field order when the company brings both evidence and a sequence people can execute. She will not trade Kest Mourne for absolution, and she will not let the siege excuse a lie that prevents a viable remedy. She can bind a temporary operational compact with Venn for this battle; permanent joint control still requires public records, civil process, and recognized Lorn witnesses. Name the reserve, crew, road, and hour a proposal requires; accusation by itself moves nothing.

## Edda's sealed answer

Six weeks ago Venn sent an original Lorn conduit plate and demanded joint inspection after Lorn's last reliable chimney failed. Edda called it enemy fabrication, sealed it beside the old minutes, and urged refusal. She does not know what has accumulated behind the southern wall. A private accusation makes her close ranks because it exposes an officer without changing any standing order.

## How Kest Mourne admits a fact

Do not resolve the city's culpability through remorse. Choose the witnesses. A finding becomes command when it is copied into all six sector ledgers, read down the command tubes, used to correct the wall map, and attached to an order that changes work already costing lives. A verified plate joined to a survivable command can force Edda to release the minutes and let six sectors act. Anything less can later be dismissed as rumor.

## Using the Court

Bring evidence here as command work: a damaged object that needs judgment, a field report that contradicts the map, or a messenger spending a final sentence on one usable fact. Each verified fact should release troops, open records, order an evacuation, or make a temporary parley executable. The Court changes the city's direction; it is not a recurring briefing room.

## If neglected

The Court remains standing and ceases to command. Rumor outruns the runners. Sector officers hoard crews and material. Edda moves the sealed minutes. A later return must restore trust or bring enough visible authority to make six defenses act as one city again.

Tamar's technical authority preserves the difference between an urgent command and work that a competent crew can actually execute.
Brann represents the Gate's demand for named reserves, defensible ground, and military time rather than an abstract claim on every city asset.
Venn's enforceable-access objective clarifies the strategic claim behind the Host without establishing any present negotiation or concession.
Bas's bounded engineering office and Heartstrike overreach explain why the enemy command can split without making its active orders known here.

encounters.title: The Shattered Gate
encounters.summary: A tower splits, six defenders signal through dust, and the Host refuses a breach it could take.
encounters.opening_view: The city's last straight beam hangs halfway into the right tower when the crack widens and traps the brace crew above it. Six defenders flash a mirror through the dust. Beneath the stair, an unexploded resonator rises in pitch with the Stone Lung. Outside, Host soldiers plant two wedges, then withdraw from a breach wide enough to enter. Brann's reserve starts toward the trapped crew; his runner points instead toward the lost gallery. The tower answers both orders by dropping its first block.
encounters.content:
## The breach

The outer doors still stand. The right tower does not. A crack runs from parapet to foundation; the upper stair is blocked, and each stroke of the Stone Lung sifts dust from the widening seam. Captain Brann Sile has shortened the line twice. One more major assault breaks it unless the tower is stabilized, the northern gallery recovered, or the defenders given room to withdraw without rout.

The Host attacks with unnerving discipline. Shield companies advance during the Lung's exhalation, plant resonant wedges, and fall back before the defenders can trap them. Twice they have refused an open way into the city. The wall is holding an army's attention while work below proceeds on schedule.

## Immediate problems

Choose the pressure that best matches current play.

- **The split tower:** A brace crew is trapped above the crack with an unexploded resonator lodged beneath it. Stabilization preserves the outer line. A fast rescue saves the crew and may cost Brann the tower.
- **The lost gallery:** Six defenders and a signal mirror are stranded behind a collapsed stair. Reaching them reveals what the Host watches between assaults.
- **The false withdrawal:** The Host leaves wounded soldiers and a broken signal slate within bowshot. The bait covers sapper work beneath the approach. Careful recovery gains prisoners and orders; pursuit spends the Gate's reserve.

No victory over the Host is required here. Save soldiers, steal minutes, and learn why the enemy will not take what the wall appears to offer.

## Brann's test

Every proposal must name what leaves Brann's wall, what that absence buys, and whether the line survives until the next assault. He accepts rescue, prediction, and controlled withdrawal as military work. Bring the assault schedule and he will abandon stone before people.

## Prisoners

A captured lower-road scout, Nara Ves, carries Venn's standing order to spare public air shafts. Her sapper escort carries Bas's later instruction to ignore that limit after the third hammer signal. Both are tired, frightened, and incomplete witnesses. Keep them alive and compare their orders. Neither knows the whole operation; together they reveal a command beginning to split.

## Defensive outcomes

A clean success delays the final assault and frees a small reserve. A costly success keeps the Gate but fixes every survivor in place. On failure, the defense falls back through two inner turns, enemy skirmishers enter the sector ring, and the Stone Lung begins with less time.

encounters.title: The Cinder Foundry
encounters.summary: A resonant shell waits in a cold furnace while the city's last skilled shift demands one named purpose.
encounters.opening_view: Mera Coil stands between a gate officer and the east furnace's ignition lever. Inside the cold furnace, a buried shell sings deeper with every stroke of the Stone Lung; nine chalk circles mark the workers already killed obeying orders around it. The last shift has divided one stock of iron into straight beams, filter frames, counterweight blanks, and an unfinished cutting rig. Tamar Ohn lowers a tuning fork. It trembles before touching stone. ‘Name the work,’ Mera says, while the officer reaches again for the lever.
encounters.content:
## Heat and cadence

Every few minutes, the unexploded shell buried in the east furnace answers the Stone Lung with a low note. Foundry Master Mera Coil has killed the furnace and cleared half the hall. Gate officers arrive with an order to relight it.

Ventwright Tamar Ohn warns that heat or one careless hammer blow may tune the red chimney to the shell. Nine workers have already died obeying siege orders. Mera will not spend a tenth crew to save an officer from waiting.

## The live shell

The shell remembers vibration. Ceramic ribs collect the Lung's cycle and return it through the surrounding stone. It can be cooled and extracted, detuned where it lies, or buried with the east furnace. Intact, it gives the cleanest frequency model. Broken, it still yields maker's marks, tolerances, and the higher setting Bas cut beyond Venn's limit.

## Competing production

After the shell is safe, one full shift of skilled labor remains before the next assault. The shift can complete one program or divide itself among reduced packages already begun:

- radial braces for the Shattered Gate;
- a cutting frame and tuned wedges for Heartstrike;
- counterweights for retuning the Stone Lung; or
- filter housings for the Pale Gardens and Refuge Galleries.

Record what is full, what is diminished, and what never leaves the floor. Imported labor, a preserved east furnace, or new iron can enlarge the shift. Without one of those, each additional order consumes another asset; it does not create more work from the same hands.

## Tamar Ohn

Tamar knows the Lung as a machine sustained by repairs, substitutions, and habits absent from every diagram. It is drawing too hard through the northern branches, yet the public plans show no southern branch to reopen. Her first answer is defensive: brace the crown, choke the unknown leak, save Kest Mourne. Old diagrams joined to measured pressure can show her a wider balance still exists.

## Mera Coil

Mera's loyalty belongs to the people who put their hands near the metal. Respect it, and she becomes the forewoman who can hold several lethal stations to one cadence. Override her, and equipment may arrive sooner, but no disciplined crew follows it below.

## If neglected

The shell splits the east furnace. The Foundry survives, but the tuning benches disappear under stone and the workers scatter. Crude repair remains possible. Every precise task at the Stone Lung becomes slower, louder, and more dangerous.

encounters.title: The Pale Gardens
encounters.summary: Poisoned tools and starving rootstock write two different disasters across the city's living filters.
encounters.opening_view: Officials with torches enter the Pale Gardens to burn every bed marked by bitter orange mold. Growers drag translucent filter trays clear while cave moths batter vents the public map calls sealed. Beneath an overturned cart, a Refuge porter clutches a message for Deren Vask; children below faint whenever the Lung draws. Sen Tahl lays two cuttings before the fire: orange growth from a sabotaged tool, colorless root from an old southern bed. One is poisoned. The other is starving. The torch descends toward both.
encounters.content:
## Two failures in one bed

Several beds have gone translucent. Black cave moths crowd vents the plans call dead. Bitter orange mold appears wherever Host infiltrators handled tools. Two frightened officials bring Sen Tahl opposite orders: burn every marked bed before the mold spreads, or keep harvesting and risk poisoning the city.

The orange mold is recent sabotage and does not match the preserved strain from the old blight. The translucent beds are starving for fresh air. One fire would consume the poison, the harvest, the living filters, and the clearest record of the Lung's failing draw.

## Separating the failures

Compare spore color, root moisture, insect behavior, and timing against the Lung's stroke. Sabotage follows hands, carts, and tool sheds. Airflow damage forms a gradient toward a sealed southern vent absent from the current plans.

Saving the Gardens may require:

- isolating and burning the poisoned beds;
- opening narrow service vents without drawing black breath into the food caverns;
- protecting growers from infiltrators and frightened soldiers; and
- keeping command from feeding filter beds to emergency furnaces.

## Sen Tahl

Sen is patient with ignorance and merciless with waste. She cares less about naming the liar of eighteen years ago than keeping enough living material to read the air tonight. Give her workers and room to act, and the Gardens become a ward-by-ward tracer. Burn the wrong beds, and she still defends the city, but brings neither filters nor reliable readings to the Lung.

## The old rootstock

Several beds descend from stock labeled for a southern exchange gallery. Their rings show that fresh flow stopped abruptly in the mold-blight year. Purge-bed labels and unfinished filter frames show that quarantine was meant to end after the contaminated flow cleared. Someone later scraped the labels and reassigned the beds. Rootstock cannot name the magistrate who made the closure permanent. It can refute the public story that Lorn's caverns failed by slow exhaustion.

## Refuge ties

Ration porters from the Refuge Galleries are trapped when quarantine closes the terraces. One carries a plea from Deren Vask, an old vent mason who recognizes the southern marks. Another reports children fainting below during the same stroke that drives moths against the sealed vents. Gardens and Refuge are breathing one failure at different depths.

## If neglected

Officials burn the suspect terraces. The sabotage dies with them. Kest Mourne loses weeks of food, its best filters, and the spores needed to judge a controlled reopening. Ration cuts begin in the Refuge before the smoke clears.

encounters.title: The Refuge Galleries
encounters.summary: Eleven missing ration sacks, a threatened witness, and forty-three omitted names turn bad air into public judgment.
encounters.opening_view: The ration cart arrives eleven sacks short, and the Refuge Galleries move as one body. Families surge toward the council stair with yellow lamps, sleeping children, and memorial tablets absent from the public wall. A relief officer grips Deren Vask's wrist. A healer adds another collapse beneath the Lung's draw column. Above them, Edda Marr's clerk carries an order to close the crypt. The missing food is blamed on the Gate; the bad air on a branch the maps deny. Someone stumbles, and the whole accusation leans downhill.
encounters.content:
## The crowd beneath the council

Eleven ration sacks are missing when the lower-gallery lamps turn yellow. Families sleep beneath civic reliefs while chalk marks divide air, water, and floor space. Conversations shorten. Children wake gasping when the Stone Lung begins its draw.

Deren Vask, a former vent mason, has accused the council of sealing Lorn's air during the mold blight. Relief officers move to arrest him for incitement as the short ration cart reaches the crowd. A quartermaster diverted the food to the Gate; the families see one policy in the missing sacks and the threatened witness.

Arrest restores silence by driving the old workers into hiding. A rush on the council stair may uncover records and destroy the command needed to use them. Protected testimony, a public accounting, or a hearing held while safer passages open can keep truth and order in the same room.

## Deren Vask

Deren laid masonry during the blight emergency. His crew was told the southern works were temporary quarantine. Afterward, supervisors reassigned Lorn's workers and ordered Kest Mourne's masons never to speak of the branch. Deren knows the service marks and the memorial stair. He does not know what now waits behind the seal.

For eighteen years he has heard his memory called age, drink, grief, or treason. Accept every claim without testing it and he becomes reckless. Test him in public, and he becomes exact.

## The memorial wall

The public memorial names the citizens killed by mold. Private family tablets name forty-three more workers, recorded only as transferred or lost on the lower road. Their families placed the tablets around an older civic service door and arranged the first signs as a ventwright mark. Grief preserved a route the records erased. Behind the memorial crypt, a narrow stair descends to the Stone Lung's southern controls.

Speaker Edda Marr arrives when command hears of the gathering. Her response depends on prior dealings: she may bring the sealed minutes and Venn's rejected conduit plate, or order the crypt shut. The minutes record a real lethal blight, a deliberate temporary seal, the expected loss of Lorn's air, the planned purge and filter works, and the later decision to keep the emergency measure after the contaminated strain died. Venn's ultimatum records the collapse of Lorn's last reliable chimney and demands inspectors from both cities at the southern controls.

## Water and gardens

Refuge healers have kept better records than the council. Fainting follows the Lung's draw, not meals. The worst cases cluster around water from the lower cistern line. Their ledgers point toward the Pale Gardens and Black Cisterns. The stewards who kept those ledgers can become the city's evacuation corps.

## If neglected

The ration dispute becomes a crush on the council stair. Deren vanishes into custody. Edda moves the minutes. Families scatter into disused passages with their lamps and records. The memorial stair remains discoverable, but no organized civilian force waits to empty the lower wards.

encounters.title: The Cisterns of Black Breath
encounters.summary: Three workers hammer beneath an oily waterline where old valves expose the lie in the city's maps.
encounters.opening_view: Three breathing hoods lie beside the Black Cisterns' inspection arch. Four people are needed below. The rescue rope has gone slack, but a trapped worker still hammers from behind the barred sluice: pressure, pause, pressure, silence. Oily water washes over valve numbers hidden beneath fresh lime. Cala Orm points from the nearest bypass to the channel feeding the Refuge Galleries. Opening it may save the crew. The Stone Lung draws, a sweet mineral breath crosses the pool, and the worker misses the next beat.
encounters.content:
## Below the waterline

Three workers are missing beyond a barred inspection arch, and an oily skin has appeared in water still feeding Kest Mourne's public pumps. Officials call it enemy poison. The smell says otherwise: mineral water, wet stone, and the faint sweetness of trapped gas.

Methane-rich black breath seeps through fractures around the southern seal. Flame can ignite it. Heavy armor and haste can carry a rescuer into air too thin for consciousness. Warn before killing: lamps extinguish in sequence, insects lie dead along a sharp boundary, and a breathing hood rests where someone understood the danger too late.

## The trapped crew

The workers closed a sluice to keep the upper supply clean. One remains conscious behind the gate and reports pressure through measured hammer taps. Reaching them preserves the city's water and a full cycle of readings. Opening the wrong bypass saves them quickly and sends black water toward the Refuge.

## The false map

Current plans show natural stone south of the fourth pool. Beneath the limewash lie old valve numbers and the chisel lines of deliberate masonry. A brass inspection plate survives in the drain. Its reverse shows one exchange system joining the Cisterns, Stone Lung, and Lorn.

The wall also explains why demolition means fire. Pressure has packed black breath behind the seal. Heartstrike will mix it with the Lung's hot release and carry ignition through both branches.

## Water Reeve Cala Orm

Cala has been accused of poisoning the city through neglect. Restoring the supply matters more to her than clearing her name. She knows the lower valves, owns several working breathing hoods, and can turn a disused overflow into a gas vent with labor and an empty gallery above. Save her crew, and she reaches the Lung as an operator. Take the map and leave them, and no one who trusts the readings remains at the controls.

## The lower-road grate

A maintenance channel behind the fourth pool opens onto an old road occupied by Host sappers. Air and water move through it in opposite phases. Follow the draft to enter the Countermine from below and hear enemy digging aimed at the Stone Lung rather than the wall.

## If neglected

The lower sluice fails. Kest Mourne keeps part of its water and loses the breathing hoods, the pressure record, and the safest vent for black breath. Refuge illness worsens. Heartstrike arms against a machine no one has measured.

encounters.title: The Countermine
encounters.summary: A collapsed lower road traps enemies together around the live cable and divided orders behind Heartstrike.
encounters.opening_view: The breakthrough drops defenders, Host sappers, and half the Countermine roof into one dust cloud. Badges vanish. Kest Mourne's miners hold a trapped sapper at blade point while enemy hands lift stone from a buried defender. Between them, a braided cable pulses toward the Stone Lung; a field tablet flashes the next hammer signal. Mael Rusk calls for a roof truce. Farther down the Host line, someone orders the cable kept live. The next pulse travels under every raised weapon.
encounters.content:
## Breakthrough

Kest Mourne's miners dig toward enemy hammers and break into an older lower road omitted from every current map. The first collapse traps defenders and Host sappers on opposite sides of a resonance cable running toward the Stone Lung. Dust erases uniforms. The next hammer signal will bring the ceiling down on everyone left in the chamber.

Begin with rescue, violence, or a shouted roof truce. Enemies who have spent nineteen days killing one another must clear the same fall, cut the same cable, exchange prisoners, or obey orders neither side fully trusts.

## The Heartstrike line

Ceramic insulators carry a braided cable deeper into the city. Its pulse matches the shells at the wall. A field tablet reduces the operation to three movements:

1. surface assaults fix Kest Mourne's reserves at the Gate and inner turns;
2. sappers expose the southern seal and place the charge; and
3. Heartstrike fractures the seal during the Lung's release.

The yield table predicts an ignition large enough to burn Kest Mourne and Lorn. Bas has marked it acceptable.

## Venn's sappers

Sap Captain Mael Rusk carries Venn's sealed order: seize the Lung and open the southern branch under control, but do not fracture it while black breath remains unvented. Bas's later valid-looking countermand cites the Host's technical articles, conceals the true yield, and tells the charge crews that delay condemns the families waiting in Lorn. Rusk holds two orders from different chains, both valid-looking, not a simple invitation to betray his marshal.

Kind words do not move him. He needs proof that Venn's controlled objective remains possible, a protected way for his crews to obey her over Bas, and assurance that Kest Mourne will not use the pause to reseal the branch. Rescue beneath the collapse, a prisoner exchange, an authenticated revocation, or a measured retuning sequence can become duty he is able to defend.

## Ways through

The commission may:

- cut the exposed cable, delaying Heartstrike and warning Bas;
- follow it covertly to the charge gallery;
- use Rusk's slate to reach Venn;
- collapse the surface branch and force a direct battle; or
- send a false completion signal while defenders reposition.

Each road gains access by spending something. Here the siege's military, technical, and political lines occupy the same narrow tunnel.

## Gate intelligence

A second tablet gives the Host's complete assault schedule, including feints and reserve timings at the Shattered Gate. Brann can save the outer line with it even if no truce survives below.

## If neglected

Bas's crews complete the charge uncontested. Venn learns its true yield only after Heartstrike begins and must oppose her own engineer under fire. The Foundry and memorial routes remain open, but prepared sappers hold the charge gallery.
