encounters.title: The Stone Lung
encounters.summary: Heartstrike turns the breathing engine into a battle for three approaches, five threatened sectors, and one military interval in which Kest Mourne and Lorn may both survive.
encounters.opening_view: The war reaches the Stone Lung before anyone does. Dust pours from the Foundry gantry; memorial ribbons snap toward Lorn's sealed branch; the Countermine tubes carry Bas's order to arm Heartstrike. Above, the Gate drum calls Brann's last reserve while Host boots answer from the lower road. Every approach delivers the soldiers, crews, witnesses, and wounds the siege left there. The first counterweight strikes its stop, and a firing signal begins moving down the ceramic ribs.
encounters.content:
## The chamber

Each stroke makes the pressure vault declare itself: loose cloth points toward the southern seal, counterweights climb into darkness, and porous vanes close around the geothermal throat. Behind a later service wall, Heartstrike ribs and cables web the southern seal; whether they are silent, charging, or under fire depends on when the company arrives. The chamber answers every intervention with pressure, heat, and movement; no one can treat it as a room between battles.

Three approaches enter the chamber.

- **The Foundry gantry** reaches the crown, counterweights, and charge harmonics. It favors bracing, disarmament, and retuning, but the Host can shell its upper supports from the Gate works.
- **The memorial stair** reaches the old civic platform and the southern branch's manual controls. It favors witnesses, evacuation, and public authority, but any mixed crew descending it is exposed to both cities' suspicion.
- **The Countermine gallery** reaches the charge and the Host assault force. It favors sabotage, parley, and direct confrontation, and it is the road Bas can reinforce fastest.

An approach is a military road, not merely an entrance. Whoever controls it can move orders, wounded, tools, and armed bodies into the Lung. Allies and enemies arrive by the roads the siege kept open, lost, or exposed.

## Arriving before Heartstrike

An early visit finds Bas still deploying the weapon. Reconnaissance can measure the Lung, reveal the southern controls, signal Venn, or cut a peripheral relay so that its silence resembles a fault. It also gives the enemy information. A missing patrol brings Host scouts. A moved valve warns Bas that the old controls have been found. A captured tube lets either command imitate the other's order.

Entering the defended charge gallery, severing the main firing cable, broadcasting a seizure, or moving the southern valves turns reconnaissance into battle. Bas then arms early and orders the Host to take whichever approach is least protected.

Before the first stroke, name the military deficit rather than an empty station: the Gate reserve committed elsewhere, a crew without an escort, civilians still in a gas path, Venn beyond signal range, or Bas holding the manual trigger. The deficit tells the GM where the enemy can force the next decision.

## Heartstrike under fire

Begin when Bas arms the charge or an intervention forces his hand. The Lung still moves on three strokes, but each stroke is also an exchange of orders and violence. Announce Bas's initiative, Venn's answer if she can give one, and the sector about to fail before the company acts. Then let the battlefield answer what they do.

### Compression: commit the reserves

The stone vanes close. Pressure rises behind the southern seal. Heartstrike charges its ceramic ribs. Bas sends assault troops through the Countermine while the Host launches its heaviest attack at the Gate. Brann must choose whether his last reserve holds the breach, escorts a technical crew, or descends to contest the charge gallery. A reserve cannot do all three.

### Draw: break the command chain

The Lung pulls through every open branch. Black breath enters cracks around the seal and moves toward occupied wards. Bas orders the southern valves pinned and the firing relays guarded. Venn may revoke him if proof and a protected signal reach her; otherwise her army continues pressing the Gate while Bas claims the chamber in Lorn's name. This stroke is won by severing, deceiving, or replacing a command chain while the gas path is turned.

### Release: survive the decision

The Lung vents through the branches still open. Heartstrike fires unless disabled, delayed, deceived, or seized. Bas reaches for the manual trigger if his crews abandon him. At the same moment the Host tries to convert any weakness at the Gate, Foundry, or Countermine into possession of the city. The chosen remedy must survive both the pressure release and an enemy attempt to take it.

The Lung may take another breath only if the defenders still hold enough ground to permit one. Each repetition costs a named sector, formation, or route: the Gate tower, the Foundry gantry, the Countermine mouth, a refuge stair, or the escort around the southern controls. Do not spend an abstract grace cycle. Show which soldiers withdraw, which road closes, and which civilians lose protection.

## Battlefronts and commands

The chamber concentrates the siege; it does not suspend it. Track the fronts that can still affect the Lung.

- **The Gate:** Brann's line buys minutes and controls the upper city road. If it falls, Host troops can descend behind the Foundry crew and Venn gains leverage at every negotiation.
- **The Foundry gantry:** Mera's workers and Tamar Ohn can brace or retune the crown, but only while an escort holds the shelling galleries and counterweight stairs.
- **The southern corridor:** Deren Vask, refuge crews, and witnesses can clear the gas path and operate the old valves. Their work decides who is warned and whether reopening is seen rather than merely promised.
- **The Countermine:** Bas's sappers, defectors, and any force sent to stop them fight over the charge, relay drums, and lower-road exit.
- **The command link:** Ilyra, Venn, Brann, and captured signal equipment determine whether troops receive one order, two contradictory orders, or none.

Ask who commands each surviving force, what road carries that command, and what enemy unit can interrupt it. Technical competence without a held road arrives too late. Military control without the right crew preserves only the weapon or the blockade.

## Korr Bas

Bas stands in the charge gallery or speaks through its tubes. He knows the ignition risk and accepts it because he believes Kest Mourne will keep Lorn dying for as long as caution remains an available excuse. Appeals to patience confirm him. A visible reopening sequence attacks the premise beneath Heartstrike; a promise made while the southern seal stays closed does not.

Venn's authenticated revocation can split his crews only when they have a protected route to obey it. If soldiers lower their weapons, Bas calls them deserters and tries to fire manually. If Kest Mourne seizes him without opening the branch, other Host officers may continue the assault under a cleaner command.

## Sera Venn

Venn continues the attack until Lorn has enforceable access to the Lung. Proof of Bas's plan stops the detonation while the claim that brought her army remains. She can order a ceasefire corridor, withdraw units from the Gate, or send trusted soldiers to hold Bas's crews apart, but each concession risks her authority while Lorn still waits for air.

She accepts a temporary truce only when reopening has begun or the company offers leverage that survives the emergency: public admission, custody divided across control keys and machinery, mixed crews physically occupying the controls, or records neither city can quietly erase. Ilyra can bind that compact for the present battle. Permanent control, reparations, prisoners, and withdrawal remain unsettled.

## Complete outcomes

### Shared retuning under truce

Venn opens a ceasefire corridor. Brann yields room for a mixed escort. Foundry and Lorn crews brace the crown, vent black breath into abandoned high galleries, fit living filters, and open the southern branch by stages while both armies watch the readings. The operation succeeds only if the truce survives Bas, a frightened defender, and the pressure release. Both settlements keep their air; neither army can claim sole possession of the controls when the stroke ends.

### Defensive reseal

Kest Mourne's forces take the charge gallery, disarm Heartstrike, collapse the lower road, and choke the southern branch permanently. The Gate can then be held or relieved. Lorn's air continues to fail. This is a military victory for Kest Mourne and the beginning of a larger war, not a repaired machine.

### Sacrificial venting

A fighting withdrawal clears an upper sector while engineers rupture its chimney and open the southern branch through the falling pressure. Lorn regains exchange. Kest Mourne loses homes, fortifications, and the population the damaged Lung can no longer sustain. The sector survives only if soldiers hold its evacuation road instead of the wall they were ordered to defend.

Other outcomes answer to the same battlefield. Destroying Heartstrike prevents one catastrophe. Killing Bas may break or harden the Host command. Silencing the Lung buys hours in which armies can still take ground. None of these acts settles who controls the next breath.

## Resolution

End when the pressure crisis and the battle reach a position no commander can immediately overturn. Name the held and lost sectors, the units that withdrew or surrendered, the road by which civilians escaped, the fate of Bas, and the order Venn gives her army.

The aftermath should look like a siege after a decision: six lanterns burning evenly with a seventh lit for Lorn while mixed sentries face outward; an upper ward dark and empty behind a new defensive line; Host prisoners carrying filters through the opened branch; or the southern controls buried while both armies prepare for another campaign.

At settlement, Ilyra reads the operational compact over the open command tubes. Edda releases duplicate minutes to the sector runners. The false southern map comes off the Court floor, a corrected plate is mounted where six commands can see it, and the southern keys pass to mixed crews who cannot turn them alone. That is Kest Mourne's admission: records, roads, and machinery no longer permit the city to restore the lie quietly. Later law can judge the blockade and the attack. The finale first decides who is alive, who holds the roads, and whether either city can still breathe.

reference_links.context: Ilyra can bind emergency operations and city forces, but the chamber still requires roads, crews, evidence, and civil acts that her office cannot manufacture.
Edda can make the corrected record a public civic act, while the finale must still determine whether the minutes are released and what orders they change.
Tamar owns competent operation and technical refusal, not the political choice among resealing, sacrifice, and shared air.
Brann's line controls military time and an upper-city road, but his presence, reserve, withdrawal, and cooperation depend on the siege state actually preserved.
Venn can bind Host strategy and an enforceable battlefield pause, but access, cooperation, unit position, and permanent terms remain outcomes of play.
Bas's authority and motive explain Heartstrike's command problem while leaving his location, manual control, crew obedience, signal state, and fate unresolved.
The commission can bind emergency movement and a temporary compact while permanent control and technically possible work remain outside its authority.
The Gate record identifies the upper-city road and military time that can reach the chamber without granting a reserve or held line.
The Foundry record identifies the gantry, tools, and skilled work without placing a crew, escort, braces, or completed equipment.
The Galleries record identifies the memorial stair, witnesses, and evacuation relationship without establishing access, attendance, or public legitimacy.
The Countermine record identifies the direct lower-road approach without fixing control, truce, sapper position, or charge access.
The Lung record owns the durable machine and three approaches while pressure, keys, roads, crews, damage, remedy, and custody remain live.
The Host record separates strategic command from technical procedure without deciding Venn’s reach, Bas’s control, or any unit’s obedience.
Heartstrike supplies the weapon architecture while its charge, cable, governor, trigger, signal, crew, and fate remain unresolved.

revelations.title: The Shattered Gate can still buy the city time
revelations.description: The tower can be braced or abandoned in order. Its outcome decides how much time and how many soldiers reach the Stone Lung.

revelations.title: The Cinder Foundry can counter the resonance weapons
revelations.description: The Foundry holds the live shell, tuned tools, and skilled crews needed to understand Heartstrike and work safely on the Lung.

revelations.title: The Pale Gardens can map and clean the failing air
revelations.description: The Gardens are recording airflow failure and can supply filters, living tracers, and a ward-by-ward map of the city's breath.

revelations.title: The Refuge Galleries hold witnesses and an old service route
revelations.description: Surviving vent masons, sealed minutes, and the memorial stair can expose the southern branch's history and reach its controls.

revelations.title: The Cisterns of Black Breath expose the false conduit map and black breath
revelations.description: Old valve marks, trapped gas, and pressure readings reveal the false map and the danger packed behind the southern seal.

revelations.title: The Countermine reaches the enemy’s true line of effort
revelations.description: The old lower road contains the Heartstrike cable, the Host's operational orders, and the fracture in its command.

revelations.title: A secured approach reaches the Stone Lung
revelations.description: The Foundry gantry, memorial stair, and Countermine gallery each provide an independent route to a different station. Discovering any one approach makes the chamber actionable; securing more approaches changes which crews, witnesses, and enemies can arrive.

revelations.title: The siege is shaping access to the Stone Lung
revelations.description: The Host's surface assaults fix Kest Mourne's defenders while sappers expose the southern seal and prepare Heartstrike below.

revelations.title: Kest Mourne sealed Lorn’s air branch and concealed it
revelations.description: Kest Mourne sealed the shared branch during the blight, knew Lorn would lose air, and falsified the public record afterward.

revelations.title: The enemy command is divided over Heartstrike
revelations.description: Venn intends controlled seizure and reopening; Bas has misused technical command to prepare a larger fracture charge despite the risk to both cities.

revelations.title: The Stone Lung can be retuned for shared air
revelations.description: The crown can be braced and the southern branch reopened if black breath is vented first, living filters are placed, and the valves move by measured stages.

revelations.title: Field evidence can change citywide orders at the Lantern Court
revelations.description: Military reports joined to physical proof give Ilyra grounds to move reserves, expose records, evacuate wards, and bind a temporary operational parley.

clues.title: The gate’s double red flare
clues.description: Brann Sile’s runner reports a split tower, an isolated gallery, and a double red flare meaning the outer line can hold only if independent help arrives before the next exhalation.
clues.discovery: Receive the gate runner while allocating the city’s remaining reserve.

clues.title: The ringing shell fragment
clues.description: A fragment brought from the wall rings in answer to the civic lanterns. Tamar Ohn identifies the Cinder Foundry as the only place able to reproduce and counter its frequency.
clues.discovery: Examine the fragment or ask why the command staff has ordered it kept away from the walls.

clues.title: The blue garden lantern
clues.description: The sector lantern linked to the Pale Gardens burns blue before any other public flame changes. Growers report translucent beds and insects clustering on sealed vents.
clues.discovery: Compare the lantern cycle with the incoming garden report.

clues.title: The impossible refuge air tally
clues.description: The lower Refuge Galleries go stale despite holding fewer people than their documented capacity. A detained former vent mason says the command map omits the branch that once ventilated them.
clues.discovery: Reconcile the refuge steward’s tally with the command map.

clues.title: The sealed black-water flask
clues.description: A cistern runner brings water with an oily skin and reports three missing crew members beyond an inspection arch where lamps will not burn.
clues.discovery: Question the runner or inspect the flask without bringing flame near it.

clues.title: Hammer signals beneath the Court
clues.description: Three sector reports place the loudest enemy hammer strokes deep inside the wall line rather than at its foundations. Kest Mourne’s Countermine is close to breaking into the same gallery.
clues.discovery: Plot the messenger reports on the command floor or listen through the old sounding bowl.

clues.title: The rejected joint-inspection packet
clues.description: Venn's original Lorn conduit plate is filed behind Edda's refusal with the old minutes. The docket dates Lorn's last auxiliary-chimney collapse six weeks earlier and shows Kest Mourne rejected inspection under the very map the plate contradicts.
clues.discovery: Press Edda to produce the sealed demand, obtain Ilyra's order to open the packet, or catch the records clerk moving it.

clues.title: Venn's authenticated revocation
clues.description: A reply through the lower-road signal chain confirms that Venn authorized controlled seizure and forbids ignition while black breath remains trapped. It specifically revokes Bas's higher-yield countermand, proving his technical order no longer represents strategic command.
clues.discovery: Open a temporary parley or route Rusk's slate and the captured orders through Ilyra's signal officers.

clues.title: The unexploded tower resonator
clues.description: The shell beneath the trapped brace crew cannot be safely struck or removed with field tools. Its maker’s geometry points to the Cinder Foundry’s tuning benches.
clues.discovery: Reach the split tower and inspect the live shell.

clues.title: The scout’s lower-road route
clues.description: Nara Ves entered through an old lower-road shaft and knows that the Host’s sapper line passes beneath the western wall toward Kest Mourne’s Countermine.
clues.discovery: Capture and question Nara, or recover her route slate from the false withdrawal.

clues.title: Brann’s consolidated defense report
clues.description: The assault timings, casualty count, and unexploded shell together justify changing the citywide reserve plan, but only Ilyra Dain can issue the necessary orders.
clues.discovery: Help Brann stabilize the line well enough to produce a reliable report.

clues.title: The assaults refuse the open breach
clues.description: Enemy companies withdraw after planting resonant wedges even when the split tower offers a momentary path inside. Their objective is timing and fixation, not immediate entry.
clues.discovery: Observe two assault cycles from the isolated gallery or compare Brann’s logs.

clues.title: Conflicting orders on the prisoners
clues.description: Venn's standing order forbids damage to public air shafts. Bas's later hammer instruction tells the sappers to ignore that limit after the third signal.
clues.discovery: Keep the captured scout and sapper alive long enough to compare their written orders.

clues.title: The split-tower brace calculation
clues.description: Mera Coil’s load model shows that three radial braces can preserve the gate’s right tower through another assault if fitted before the next compression stroke.
clues.discovery: Ask the foundry to model the cracked tower or compare its measurements with the recovered shell damage.

clues.title: The unfinished filter-frame requisition
clues.description: Tamar’s abandoned work order calls for living filter mats and spore tracers from the Pale Gardens to test the ventilation frame before it is installed.
clues.discovery: Review Tamar’s competing production orders or inspect the half-built frame.

clues.title: The counterweight service gantry
clues.description: A sealed hoistway behind the counterweight stores descends directly to the Stone Lung's crown. Its service plate marks it as one independent approach among the crown, civic-control, and lower-road routes.
clues.discovery: Trace the old counterweight chains or obtain Tamar Ohn’s maintenance key.

clues.title: The shell frequency model
clues.description: The recovered resonator is inefficient against ordinary walls but precisely tuned to the Stone Lung’s release frequency. The surface bombardment is calibration for a deeper target.
clues.discovery: Extract or detune the live shell and reproduce its cadence on the tuning bench.

clues.title: The erased safety tolerance
clues.description: The shell's original maker marks include a maximum safe charge bearing Venn's seal. Bas's later technical countermand cuts away that limit and substitutes a larger setting never approved by strategic command.
clues.discovery: Clean the ceramic ribs intact enough to compare the two sets of marks.

clues.title: The variable-vane model
clues.description: A scale reconstruction shows the crown accepting a new balance when the southern branch opens by stages, the trapped gas is vented first, and living filters protect the restored exchange.
clues.discovery: Combine the shell frequency with Tamar’s surviving counterweight specifications.

clues.title: Mera's signed production board
clues.description: The foundry board names exactly what one remaining shift can finish and which sector loses each diverted beam, filter housing, or counterweight. With Mera's signature, Ilyra can reissue the reserve plan without pretending the city has materials it does not.
clues.discovery: Settle the production allocation with Mera and preserve enough of the benches to certify the remaining capacity.

clues.title: The cracked foundry exhaust
clues.description: Each draw stroke pulls soot backward through a cracked foundry exhaust and across the translucent beds. Growers report a deep ringing there that began with the latest bombardment.
clues.discovery: Follow the soot gradient instead of assuming every damaged bed was poisoned.

clues.title: Deren Vask’s ration-cart message
clues.description: A trapped ration porter carries Deren’s request that someone compare the southern rootstock marks with the memorial records in the Refuge Galleries.
clues.discovery: Release the quarantined porters or inspect the message hidden in the cart tally.

clues.title: The growers’ living air map
clues.description: Sen Tahl's full-cycle map shows which wards fail on each stroke and where evacuation crews and filters must stand when the Lung changes.
clues.discovery: Preserve enough beds and insect observations to complete one full-cycle map.

clues.title: The southern rootstock gradient
clues.description: Old filter beds labeled for the southern exchange stopped receiving fresh flow abruptly in the mold-blight year. Purge-bed marks show the quarantine was designed to end, not become a permanent diversion.
clues.discovery: Compare surviving rootstock rings and scraped bed labels across the terraces.

clues.title: The spore-tracer sequence
clues.description: Different spores move on compression, draw, and release. Garden crews can mark the black-breath front and confirm when the southern valves may advance safely.
clues.discovery: Separate sabotage from suffocation and run controlled tracers through the service vents.

clues.title: The refuge healers’ breathing ledger
clues.description: Fainting follows the Lung’s draw and worsens when the Pale Gardens’ filter beds are offline. The healers’ timing can be tested against the gardens’ insects and spores.
clues.discovery: Review the symptom ledger rather than treating the illness as hunger or panic.

clues.title: The oily-water sickness cluster
clues.description: The worst headaches and lamp failures occur among families drawing from the lower cistern line. Their water develops an oily skin minutes before the air turns bad.
clues.discovery: Compare family water sources with the healers’ ward map.

clues.title: The memorial maintenance stair
clues.description: The family tablets preserve a ventwright mark around an older service door. The stair behind it descends independently to the Stone Lung's southern controls, separate from the crown and lower-road approaches.
clues.discovery: Reconcile the public memorial with the private family tablets and follow Deren’s service symbols.

clues.title: The sealed minutes and Deren’s testimony
clues.description: The minutes and Deren's account agree: Kest Mourne sealed the shared branch temporarily, knew Lorn would lose air, abandoned the planned purge and filter works, and hid the permanent closure after the blight died out.
clues.discovery: Protect Deren’s testimony and obtain or publicly compel the sealed council minutes.

clues.title: The ventwrights' three-stage litany
clues.description: The family tablets preserve a maintenance litany: clear the dead air, steady the crown, then wake the southern leaves one mark at a time. Deren recognizes it as the old safe sequence for reopening a quarantined exchange.
clues.discovery: Read the memorial arrangement with Deren or compare its repeated marks to the sealed minutes.

clues.title: The public refuge hearing record
clues.description: A named transcript joins Deren's testimony, the healers' timing ledger, the sealed minutes, and Venn's rejected plate before families and relief officers. Once copied, Ilyra can order disclosure, evacuation, and a parley without resting the decision on one hidden witness.
clues.discovery: Hold a public accounting that protects Deren and keeps the ration dispute from becoming a crush.

clues.title: The old refuge evacuation marks
clues.description: Valve numbers beneath the limewash match service symbols used in the Refuge memorial crypt, where surviving blight workers and the sealed record can interpret them.
clues.discovery: Expose the older markings around the false southern dead end.

clues.title: The lower-road maintenance grate
clues.description: A drainage channel opens into the old lower road. Enemy hammer strokes and resonance cable pulses carry through it toward Kest Mourne’s Countermine.
clues.discovery: Follow the opposing movement of air and water behind the fourth pool.

clues.title: The original conduit plate
clues.description: The brass plate, gas readings, and deliberate masonry give Ilyra proof strong enough to overrule the public map and issue citywide orders.
clues.discovery: Recover the plate and one complete pressure cycle without igniting the chamber.

clues.title: The hidden masonry and original map
clues.description: Chisel marks show a built closure where the current map claims natural stone. The original inspection diagram names Lorn as the southern exchange branch.
clues.discovery: Strip the limewash and inspect the reverse of the surviving conduit plate.

clues.title: The pressure and valve readings
clues.description: Cala Orm’s measurements identify a disused overflow that can vent the black breath and give the pressure limits for opening the southern valves in stages.
clues.discovery: Rescue the trapped crew or reproduce their hammer readings across a full Lung cycle.

clues.title: The full gate assault tablet
clues.description: The sapper tablet lists the Host’s feints, reserve commitments, and the exact release stroke chosen for the next major attack on the Shattered Gate.
clues.discovery: Capture the field tablet or obtain it from Mael Rusk during a local truce.

clues.title: The black-breath drainage draft
clues.description: A sweet, dead draft enters the old road through a submerged maintenance grate. Enemy sappers avoid it and mark the connection to Kest Mourne’s lower cisterns.
clues.discovery: Trace the draft or read the hazard marks on the sapper plan.

clues.title: The Heartstrike cable
clues.description: The resonance cable runs directly from the sapper line to a charge gallery behind the Stone Lung's southern seal. It provides an independent lower-road approach to the chamber's armed station.
clues.discovery: Follow, tap, or map the cable after the breakthrough.

clues.title: The Heartstrike operational plan
clues.description: The written plan states that surface assaults exist to fix reserves while the lower-road crews expose and fracture the southern seal during the Lung’s release.
clues.discovery: Recover Bas’s field tablet from the trapped sapper chamber.

clues.title: Venn’s limits and Bas’s countermand
clues.description: Rusk carries Venn's order for controlled seizure beside Bas's valid-looking technical countermand to arm Heartstrike at a concealed higher yield. The orders come from different chains and cannot both be obeyed safely.
clues.discovery: Compare the sap captain’s sealed orders or establish a direct signal to Venn.

clues.title: Rusk's protected truce slate
clues.description: Rusk's slate names the crews willing to obey Venn, the route by which they can withdraw from Bas, and the conditions under which they will protect controlled reopening. It gives Ilyra something operational to order, not merely an enemy promise.
clues.discovery: Rescue the trapped sappers, authenticate Venn's limits, and negotiate a protected route for Rusk's crews.

clues.title: The assault relay drum
clues.description: A relay drum beside Heartstrike carries three surface signals into the charge gallery: Gate fixation, reserve displacement, and southern-seal readiness. Its teeth advance only when the outer assault has drawn defenders away from the lower road.
clues.discovery: Inspect the charge-gallery relays before arming, intercept a signal cycle, or compare the drum to the Countermine operation table.

clues.title: The buried Lorn control ring
clues.description: Behind the later service wall, the original southern-control ring bears both Kest Mourne and Lorn custody marks. Newer masonry covers Lorn's half, while replacement index plates reroute the branch into a blank stone sector.
clues.discovery: Open the false wall carefully enough to preserve the original controls and compare their marks with the current map.

clues.title: The bypassed command governor
clues.description: Heartstrike's firing assembly includes Venn's sealed safety governor, designed to block fracture at the measured gas pressure. Bas has bridged it with a hand-cut ceramic shunt and wired the manual trigger outside the strategic command lock.
clues.discovery: Reach the charge gallery intact, inspect the firing assembly, or force Bas's crew to explain why the governor no longer controls the charge.

clues.title: The surviving balance marks
clues.description: Original score marks on the crown and southern valves record stable paired settings that include flow toward Lorn. They confirm the Lung was built to balance both branches and can accept staged reopening once pressure and gas are controlled.
clues.discovery: Study a full cycle from the crown and southern controls, or align the old marks with Tamar's model and Cala's readings.
